title: S. C. Bradford
description: A librarian at London's Science Museum Library, Bradford formulates Bradford's Law describing how articles on a subject scatter across journals — foundational to how libraries built collections and indexes.

title: Eugene Garfield
description: Holding a Master's in Library Science from Columbia, Garfield proposes citation indexing in Science, then founds the Institute for Scientific Information (1960) and publishes the first Science Citation Index (1964).

title: Alan Pritchard
description: Writing in the Journal of Documentation, a library and information science journal, Pritchard coins the term "bibliometrics," giving the field its lasting name.

title: Henry Small
description: A joint PhD in chemistry and history of science working as chief scientist at the Institute for Scientific Information, Small develops co-citation analysis, mapping how the literature clusters around shared ideas.
